title: Karma-Sannyāsa Yoga
subtitle: Path of Renunciation
theme: Krishna reconciles the paths of self-less action and inward renunciation, showing that both converge in the peace of Brahman-realisation.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि।

यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम्।।5.1।।
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sannyāsaṁ karmaṇāṁ kṛiṣhṇa punar yogaṁ cha śhansasi
yach chhreya etayor ekaṁ tan me brūhi su-niśhchitam
verses.wordMeanings: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; sanyāsam—renunciation; karmaṇām—of actions; kṛiṣhṇa—Shree Krishna; punaḥ—again; yogam—about karm yog; cha—also; śhansasi—you praise; yat—which; śhreyaḥ—more beneficial; etayoḥ—of the two; ekam—one; tat—that; me—unto me; brūhi—please tell; su-niśhchitam—conclusively

translation.english: Arjuna said: Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions, and again you praise yoga in action. Tell me decisively which of the two is superior.
translation.hindi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे कृष्ण, आप कभी कर्मों के संन्यास की प्रशंसा करते हैं और फिर कर्मयोग की। इन दोनों में श्रेष्ठ क्या है, मुझे निश्चयपूर्वक बताइए।

explanation.english: Arjuna still feels torn between the quiet life of a renunciant and the active life of a warrior-yogi; he now presses Krishna for a single, clear verdict.
explanation.hindi: अर्जुन अब भी त्याग-मय निष्क्रिय जीवन और कर्म-प्रधान सक्रिय जीवन के बीच उलझा है; वह कृष्ण से एक स्पष्ट, निर्णायक उत्तर मांगता है।

verses.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ।

तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते।।5.2।।
verses.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
sannyāsaḥ karma-yogaśh cha niḥśhreyasa-karāvubhau
tayos tu karma-sannyāsāt karma-yogo viśhiṣhyate
verses.wordMeanings: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha—the Supreme Lord said; sanyāsaḥ—renunciation; karma-yogaḥ—working in devotion; cha—and; niḥśhreyasa-karau—lead to the supreme goal; ubhau—both; tayoḥ—of the two; tu—but; karma-sanyāsāt—renunciation of actions; karma-yogaḥ—working in devotion; viśhiṣhyate—is superior

translation.english: The Blessed Lord said: Both renunciation and karma-yoga lead to the supreme good, but of the two, karma-yoga is superior to mere renunciation.
translation.hindi: भगवान ने कहा: संन्यास और कर्मयोग दोनों परम कल्याणकारी हैं, परंतु इन दोनों में कर्मसंन्यास की अपेक्षा कर्मयोग श्रेष्ठ है।

explanation.english: Krishna affirms the equal goal but different practicability: inward detachment while acting (karma-yoga) is safer than physical withdrawal for the majority.
explanation.hindi: कृष्ण लक्ष्य की समानता पर मुहर लगाते हैं पर व्यावहारिकता को अलग करते हैं—अधिकतर साधकों के लिये कर्म में निरासक्ति रूपी कर्मयोग भौतिक संन्यास से सुगम है।

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति।

निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते।।5.3।।
verses.transliteration:
jñeyaḥ sa nitya-sannyāsī yo na dveṣhṭi na kāṅkṣhati
nirdvandvo hi mahā-bāho sukhaṁ bandhāt pramuchyate
verses.wordMeanings: jñeyaḥ—should be considered; saḥ—that person; nitya—always; sanyāsī—practising renunciation; yaḥ—who; na—never; dveṣhṭi—hate; na—nor; kāṅkṣhati—desire; nirdvandvaḥ—free from all dualities; hi—certainly; mahā-bāho—mighty-armed one; sukham—easily; bandhāt—from bondage; pramuchyate—is liberated

translation.english: Know him to be a perpetual renunciant who neither hates nor desires. Free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily released from bondage.
translation.hindi: जो न द्वेष करता है न कामना, उसे नित्य संन्यासी जानो। हे महाबाहो, द्वंद्वों से रहित मनुष्य सहज ही बंधन से मुक्त हो जाता है।

explanation.english: Real renunciation is an attitude, not an external status; when aversion and craving end, freedom dawns whether one is in a cave or on a battlefield.
explanation.hindi: वास्तविक संन्यास बाहरी वेश नहीं, भीतरी अवस्था है; द्वेष-कामना मिटते ही, गुफा हो या रणक्षेत्र—मुक्ति अपने-आप खिलती है।

verses.sanskrit:
सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः।

एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम्।।5.4।।
verses.transliteration:
sānkhya-yogau pṛithag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ
ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyag ubhayor vindate phalam
verses.wordMeanings: sānkhya—renunciation of actions; yogau—karm yog; pṛithak—different; bālāḥ—the ignorant; pravadanti—say; na—never; paṇḍitāḥ—the learned; ekam—in one; api—even; āsthitaḥ—being situated; samyak—completely; ubhayoḥ—of both; vindate—achieve; phalam—the result

translation.english: Childish people speak of Sāṅkhya (the path of knowledge) and yoga (the path of action) as distinct; not the wise. Whoever is firmly established in either gains the fruit of both.
translation.hindi: बालक लोग सांख्य और योग को भिन्न कहते हैं, पंडित नहीं। जो किसी एक में भी सम्यक् स्थित हो, वह दोनों का फल पाता है।

explanation.english: Krishna removes the conceptual split: knowledge without selfless action is sterile; action without wisdom is blind. Integrated practice yields the same realisation.
explanation.hindi: कृष्ण वैचारिक फांकों को पाटते हैं: निष्काम कर्म रहित ज्ञान बंजर है, विवेक रहित कर्म अंधा है। एकीकृत साधना वही परम सिद्धि देती है।

verses.sanskrit:
यत्सांख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते।

एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति।।5.5।।
verses.transliteration:
yat sānkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṁ tad yogair api gamyate
ekaṁ sānkhyaṁ cha yogaṁ cha yaḥ paśhyati sa paśhyati
verses.wordMeanings: yat—what; sānkhyaiḥ—by means of karm sanyās; prāpyate—is attained; sthānam—place; tat—that; yogaiḥ—by working in devotion; api—also; gamyate—is attained; ekam—one; sānkhyam—renunciation of actions; cha—and; yogam—karm yog; cha—and; yaḥ—who; paśhyati—sees; saḥ—that person; paśhyati—actually sees

translation.english: The state reached by the Sāṅkhya path is also attained by the yoga path. Truly sees who sees Sāṅkhya and yoga as one.
translation.hindi: जो स्थान सांख्य से प्राप्त होता है, वही योगियों द्वारा भी प्राप्त होता है। सांख्य और योग को एक ही देखने वाला ही वास्तविक दृष्टा है।

explanation.english: Whether through contemplative insight or selfless engagement, the destination—Brahman-realisation—is identical; clinging to labels blinds one to this unity.
explanation.hindi: चिन्तन-प्रधान दृष्टि हो या कर्म-प्रधान संलग्नता, मंज़िल ब्रह्म-साक्षात्कार ही है; नाम-पट्टों से चिपटना इस एकता को ओझल कर देता है।

verses.sanskrit:
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः।

योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।5.6।।
verses.transliteration:
sannyāsas tu mahā-bāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ
yoga-yukto munir brahma na chireṇādhigachchhati
verses.wordMeanings: sanyāsaḥ—renunciation; tu—but; mahā-bāho—mighty-armed one; duḥkham—distress; āptum—attains; ayogataḥ—without karm yog; yoga-yuktaḥ—one who is adept in karm yog; muniḥ—a sage; brahma—Brahman; na chireṇa—quickly; adhigachchhati—goes

translation.english: But renunciation without yoga is hard to perfect, O mighty-armed; the sage harmonised with yoga quickly attains Brahman.
translation.hindi: हे महाबाहो, योग रहित संन्यास दुःखरूप है; योगयुक्त मुनि शीघ्र ही ब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।

explanation.english: Dropping outer duties without inner mastery breeds restlessness; combining action with mindfulness ripens faster into liberation.
explanation.hindi: बाहरी कर्तव्य छोड़ना पर भीतरी साधना न होना अशांति बढ़ाता है; कर्म को सजगता से जोड़ना मुक्ति को शीघ्र परिपक्व करता है।

verses.sanskrit:
योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः।

सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते।।5.7।।
verses.transliteration:
yoga-yukto viśhuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ
sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtātmā kurvann api na lipyate
verses.wordMeanings: yoga-yuktaḥ—united in consciousness with God; viśhuddha-ātmā—one with purified intellect; vijita-ātmā—one who has conquered the mind; jita-indriyaḥ—having conquered the senses; sarva-bhūta-ātma-bhūta-ātmā—one who sees the Soul of all souls in every living being; kurvan—performing; api—although; na—never; lipyate—entangled

translation.english: The yogi of pure mind, self-controlled and conqueror of the senses, seeing the Self in all beings, is not tainted though acting.
translation.hindi: योगयुक्त, शुद्धात्मा, आत्मविजयी, इन्द्रियजीत, जो सब प्राणियों में आत्मा को देखता है, कर्म करता हुआ भी लिप्त नहीं होता।

explanation.english: Purity, mastery, and universal vision together insulate action from creating new bondage.
explanation.hindi: शुद्धता, स्व-नियंत्रण और सर्वात्म-दृष्टि जब संगठित हों तो कर्म नए बंधन नहीं रचता।

verses.sanskrit:
नैव किंचित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित्।

पश्यन् श्रृणवन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन् श्वसन्।।5.8।।
verses.transliteration:
naiva kiñchit karomīti yukto manyeta tattva-vit
paśhyañ śhṛiṇvan spṛiśhañjighrann aśhnangachchhan svapañśhvasan
 pralapan visṛijan gṛihṇann unmiṣhan nimiṣhann api
indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣhu vartanta iti dhārayan
verses.wordMeanings:
na—not; eva—certainly; kiñchit—anything; karomi—I do; iti—thus; yuktaḥ—steadfast in karm yog; manyeta—thinks; tattva-vit—one who knows the truth; paśhyan—seeing; śhṛiṇvan—hearing; spṛiśhan—touching; jighran—smelling; aśhnan—eating; gachchhan—moving; svapan—sleeping; śhvasan—breathing;
 pralapan—talking; visṛijan—giving up; gṛihṇan—accepting; unmiṣhan—opening (the eyes); nimiṣhan—closing (the eyes); api—although; indriyāṇi—the senses; indriya-artheṣhu—in sense-objects; vartante—moving; iti—thus; dhārayan—convinced

translation.english: The knower of truth, established in yoga, thinks, ‘I do nothing at all,’ seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing—
translation.hindi: योगयुक्त तत्त्वदर्शी यह मानता है—‘मैं कुछ भी नहीं करता’, चाहे वह देखता, सुनता, छूता, सूंघता, खाता, चलता, सोता या श्वास लेता हो—

explanation.english: With the ego-knot severed, daily functions are witnessed as nature’s play, not ‘mine’.
explanation.hindi: अहं-गांठ कटते ही, रोजमर्रा की क्रियाएँ प्रकृति का नाटक दिखती हैं, ‘मेरा’ कर्म नहीं।

verses.sanskrit:
प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन्।।5.9।।
verses.transliteration: pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇann unmiṣan nimiṣann api indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan
verses.wordMeanings: pralapan—by talking; visṛjan—by giving up; gṛhṇan—by accepting; unmiṣan—opening; nimiṣan—closing; api—in spite of; indriyāṇi—the senses; indriya-artheṣu—in sense gratification;   vartante—let    them be so engaged; iti—thus;   dhārayan—considering.

translation.english: Speaking, releasing, grasping, opening and closing the eyes—convinced that the senses move among their objects, he remains detached.
translation.hindi: बोलते, त्यागते, ग्रहण करते, आँखें खोलते-मूँदते समय भी वह जानता है कि इन्द्रियाँ इन्द्रिय-विषयों में चल रही हैं—वह असंग रहता है।

explanation.english: The sense-object interplay is impersonal; the yogi stands as uninvolved awareness.
explanation.hindi: इन्द्रिय-विषय की क्रिया निर्लिप्त है; योगी साक्षी-चेतना बनकर रहता है।

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः।

लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा।।5.10।।
verses.transliteration:
brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ
lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā
verses.wordMeanings: brahmaṇi—to God; ādhāya—dedicating; karmāṇi—all actions; saṅgam—attachment; tyaktvā—abandoning; karoti—performs; yaḥ—who; lipyate—is affected; na—never; saḥ—that person; pāpena—by sin; padma-patram—a lotus leaf; iva—like; ambhasā—by water

translation.english: He who dedicates actions to Brahman, abandoning attachment, is not tainted by evil—just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
translation.hindi: जो कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित कर, आसक्ति त्यागकर कर्म करता है, वह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता—जैसे जल कमल-पत्र को नहीं भिगोता।

explanation.english: Offering the doer-ship to the Absolute turns worldly work into sacred play, leaving no stain.
explanation.hindi: कर्तृत्व को परमात्मा को समर्पित कर देना सांसारिक काम को भी पावन लीला बना देता है—दाग नहीं लगता।

verses.sanskrit:
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि।

योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये।।5.11।।
verses.transliteration:
kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api
yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṁ tyaktvātma-śhuddhaye
verses.wordMeanings: kāyena—with the body; manasā—with the mind; buddhyā—with the intellect; kevalaiḥ—only; indriyaiḥ—with the senses; api—even; yoginaḥ—the yogis; karma—actions; kurvanti—perform; saṅgam—attachment; tyaktvā—giving up; ātma—of the self; śhuddhaye—for the purification

translation.english: Yogis perform action with body, mind, intellect, and senses only, abandoning attachment, for self-purification.
translation.hindi: योगी शरीर, मन, बुद्धि और मात्र इन्द्रियों से ही, आसक्ति त्यागकर, आत्म-शुद्धि के लिए कर्म करते हैं।

explanation.english: Action becomes a laboratory for inner cleansing when free from egoic claim.
explanation.hindi: अहंकार से रहित होने पर कर्म आत्म-परिष्कार की प्रयोगशाला बन जाता है।

verses.sanskrit:
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम्।

अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते।।5.12।।
verses.transliteration:
yuktaḥ karma-phalaṁ tyaktvā śhāntim āpnoti naiṣhṭhikīm
ayuktaḥ kāma-kāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate
verses.wordMeanings: yuktaḥ—one who is united in consciousness with God; karma-phalam—the results of all activities; tyaktvā—giving up; śhāntim—peace; āpnoti—attains; naiṣhṭhikīm—everlasting; ayuktaḥ—one who is not united with God in consciousness; kāma-kāreṇa—impelled by desires; phale—in the result; saktaḥ—attached; nibadhyate—becomes entangled

translation.english: The united one, abandoning the fruit of action, attains unshakable peace; the unsteady one, attached to fruit, is bound by craving.
translation.hindi: फल का त्यागकर युक्त पुरुष नैष्ठिकी शान्ति पाता है; अयुक्त, फल में आसक्त होकर, कामना के कारण बँध जाता है।

explanation.english: The axis of bondage and freedom is not action itself but the motive. Without ‘what-do-I-get’ thinking, peace happens.
explanation.hindi: बंध या मुक्ति का केन्द्रीय बिंदु कर्म नहीं, उसकी प्रेरणा है। ‘मुझे क्या मिलेगा’ मिटते ही शांति स्वतः आती है।

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी।

नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन्।।5.13।।
verses.transliteration:
sarva-karmāṇi manasā sannyasyāste sukhaṁ vaśhī
nava-dvāre pure dehī naiva kurvan na kārayan
verses.wordMeanings: sarva—all; karmāṇi—activities; manasā—by the mind; sannyasya—having renounced; āste—remains; sukham—happily; vaśhī—the self-controlled; nava-dvāre—of nine gates; pure—in the city; dehī—the embodied being; na—never; eva—certainly; kurvan—doing anything; na—not; kārayan—causing to be done

translation.english: Mentally renouncing all actions, the self-controlled indweller dwells happily in the city of nine gates, neither acting nor causing to act.
translation.hindi: मन से समस्त कर्मों का संन्यास कर, वशी देही नव-द्वार वाले शरीर-नगर में सुख से रहता है—न स्वयं करता है न कराता है।

explanation.english: ‘City of nine gates’ = the body. When mastery dawns, the inner resident remains a calm spectator, letting the bodily mechanisms run their course.
explanation.hindi: ‘नव-द्वार-पूर’ अर्थात शरीर। स्व-नियंत्रण आने पर अंत:वासी शांत दर्शक बन रहता है, शरीर-यंत्र अपनी लय में चलता है।

verses.sanskrit:
न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः।

न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते।।5.14।।
verses.transliteration:
na kartṛitvaṁ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛijati prabhuḥ
na karma-phala-saṅyogaṁ svabhāvas tu pravartate
verses.wordMeanings: na—neither; kartṛitvam—sense of doership; na—nor; karmāṇi—actions; lokasya—of the people; sṛijati—creates; prabhuḥ—God; na—nor; karma-phala—fruits of actions; sanyogam—connection; svabhāvaḥ—one’s nature; tu—but; pravartate—is enacted

translation.english: The Lord creates neither agency nor actions nor the link between action and fruit; nature alone moves.
translation.hindi: प्रभु न कर्तृत्व रचता है, न कर्म, न कर्म-फल का संयोग; केवल स्वभाव (प्रकृति) कार्य करता है।

explanation.english: Doer-ship is a superimposition; cosmic law, not an external deity, welds deeds and their outcomes.
explanation.hindi: कर्तृत्व आरोपित है; कर्म-फल का बंधन बाहरी ईश्वर नहीं, स्वयं प्रकृति का नियामक नियम है।

verses.sanskrit:
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः।

अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः।।5.15।।
verses.transliteration:
nādatte kasyachit pāpaṁ na chaiva sukṛitaṁ vibhuḥ
ajñānenāvṛitaṁ jñānaṁ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ
verses.wordMeanings: na—not; ādatte—accepts; kasyachit—anyone’s; pāpam—sin; na—not; cha—and; eva—certainly; su-kṛitam—virtuous deeds; vibhuḥ—the omnipresent God; ajñānena—by ignorance; āvṛitam—covered; jñānam—knowledge; tena—by that; muhyanti—are deluded; jantavaḥ—the living entities

translation.english: The all-pervading takes no one’s sin or virtue. Knowledge is veiled by ignorance; beings are thereby deluded.
translation.hindi: व्योमय प्रभु किसी का पाप या पुण्य ग्रहण नहीं करता; पर अज्ञान से ज्ञान आच्छादित होने से प्राणी मोहित होते हैं।

explanation.english: Individual confusion—not divine partiality—accounts for bondage. When the veil lifts, the self ever-pure is rediscovered.
explanation.hindi: बंध का कारण ईश्वरीय पक्षपात नहीं, व्यक्तिगत अज्ञान है। आवरण हटते ही शुद्ध आत्मा स्वयं प्रकट हो जाती है।

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः।

तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम्।।5.16।।
verses.transliteration:
jñānena tu tad ajñānaṁ yeṣhāṁ nāśhitam ātmanaḥ
teṣhām āditya-vaj jñānaṁ prakāśhayati tat param
verses.wordMeanings: jñānena—by divine knowledge; tu—but; tat—that; ajñānam—ignorance; yeṣhām—whose; nāśhitam—has been destroyed; ātmanaḥ—of the self; teṣhām—their; āditya-vat—like the sun; jñānam—knowledge; prakāśhayati—illumines; tat—that; param—Supreme Entity

translation.english: But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the Self, that knowledge reveals the Supreme like the sun.
translation.hindi: पर जिनका अज्ञान आत्म-ज्ञान से नष्ट हो गया है, उनके लिए वह ज्ञान सूर्य के समान परम को प्रकाशित करता है।

explanation.english: Revelation is automatic: remove the cloud (ignorance) and the ever-shining sun (Brahman) blazes forth.
explanation.hindi: प्रकाश अपने-आप होता है: बादल हटाएँ (अज्ञान) और सदा दीप्त सूर्य (ब्रह्म) प्रकट हो उठता है।

verses.sanskrit:
तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः।

गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः।।5.17।।
verses.transliteration:
tad-buddhayas tad-ātmānas tan-niṣhṭhās tat-parāyaṇāḥ
gachchhantyapunar-āvṛittiṁ jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣhāḥ
verses.wordMeanings: tat-buddhayaḥ—those whose intellect is directed toward God; tat-ātmānaḥ—those whose heart (mind and intellect) is solely absorbed in God; tat-niṣhṭhāḥ—those whose intellect has firm faith in God; tat-parāyaṇāḥ—those who strive after God as the supreme goal and refuge; gachchhanti—go; apunaḥ-āvṛittim—not returning; jñāna—by knowledge; nirdhūta—dispelled; kalmaṣhāḥ—sins

translation.english: Those whose intellects are fixed on That, who have That as the Self, who stand in That, whose supreme goal is That—purified by knowledge, they go to non-return.
translation.hindi: जिनकी बुद्धि, आत्मा, निष्ठा और परम गंतव्य वही ‘तत्’ है, ज्ञान द्वारा पापरहित वे अप्रत्यावर्तन को पहुँचते हैं।

explanation.english: Single-pointed absorption (‘tad…’) burns the seeds of rebirth; once awakened, they do not fall back.
explanation.hindi: एकनिष्ठ अवधान (‘तद…’) जन्म-बीज भस्म कर देता है; जागरण के बाद पतन नहीं।

verses.sanskrit:
विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि।

शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः।।5.18।।
verses.transliteration:
vidyā-vinaya-sampanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini
śhuni chaiva śhva-pāke cha paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśhinaḥ
verses.wordMeanings: vidyā—divine knowledge; vinaya—humbleness; sampanne—equipped with; brāhmaṇe—a Brahmin; gavi—a cow; hastini—an elephant; śhuni—a dog; cha—and; eva—certainly; śhva-pāke—a dog-eater; cha—and; paṇḍitāḥ—the learned; sama-darśhinaḥ—see with equal vision

translation.english: Sages see with equal vision a learned humble Brāhmaṇa, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and a dog-eater.
translation.hindi: ज्ञानी समदर्शी ब्राह्मण (विद्या-विनयसम्पन्न), गौ, हाथी, कुत्ते और चाण्डाल (कुत्ते-भक्षी) को समान देखते हैं।

explanation.english: Real wisdom levels the social and species hierarchy; the same Self shines in all embodiments.
explanation.hindi: सच्चा ज्ञान जाति-प्राणि भेद समापता है; प्रत्येक देह में वही एक आत्मा झलकती है।

verses.sanskrit:
इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः।

निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः।।5.19।।
verses.transliteration:
ihaiva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣhāṁ sāmye sthitaṁ manaḥ
nirdoṣhaṁ hi samaṁ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ
verses.wordMeanings: iha eva—in this very life; taiḥ—by them; jitaḥ—conquer; sargaḥ—the creation; yeṣhām—whose; sāmye—in equanimity; sthitam—situated; manaḥ—mind; nirdoṣham—flawless; hi—certainly; samam—in equality; brahma—God; tasmāt—therefore; brahmaṇi—in the Absolute Truth; te—they; sthitāḥ—are seated

translation.english: Even here they conquer birth whose mind is balanced. Spotless indeed is Brahman and the same; therefore they abide in Brahman.
translation.hindi: जिनका मन समता में स्थित है, उन्होंने यहीं जन्म-चक्र जीत लिया। ब्रह्म निर्दोष और सम है; इसलिए वे ब्रह्म में स्थित हैं।

explanation.english: Equality of vision is liberation-now; samsāra ends when preferences end.
explanation.hindi: समदृष्टि ही जीवन-मुक्ति है; राग-द्वेष मिटते ही संसार-चक्र टूट जाता है।

verses.sanskrit:
न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम्।

स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः।।5.20।।
verses.transliteration:
na prahṛiṣhyet priyaṁ prāpya nodvijet prāpya chāpriyam
sthira-buddhir asammūḍho brahma-vid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ
verses.wordMeanings: na—neither; prahṛiṣhyet—rejoice; priyam—the pleasant; prāpya—obtaining; na—nor; udvijet—become disturbed; prāpya—attaining; cha—also; apriyam—the unpleasant; sthira-buddhiḥ—steady intellect; asammūḍhaḥ—firmly situated; brahma-vit—having a firm understanding of divine knowledge; brahmaṇi—established in God; sthitaḥ—situated

translation.english: He who neither delights on obtaining the pleasant nor grieves on parting with it, steady in understanding and undeluded, knower of Brahman, abides in Brahman.
translation.hindi: प्रिय वस्तु मिलने पर हर्षित न हो, प्रिय से बिछुड़ने पर विचलित न हो—ऐसी स्थिर बुद्धि, मोह-रहित, ब्रह्म-ज्ञानी ब्रह्म में स्थित रहता है।

explanation.english: Emotional evenness signals established knowledge; ups and downs belong to the mind, not the Self.
explanation.hindi: भाव-समत्व जड़े हुए ज्ञान का सूचक है; उतार-चढ़ाव मन के हैं, आत्मा के नहीं।

verses.sanskrit:
बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम्।

स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते।।5.21।।
verses.transliteration:
bāhya-sparśheṣhvasaktātmā vindatyātmani yat sukham
sa brahma-yoga-yuktātmā sukham akṣhayam aśhnute
verses.wordMeanings: bāhya-sparśheṣhu—external sense pleasure; asakta-ātmā—those who are unattached; vindati—find; ātmani—in the self; yat—which; sukham—bliss; saḥ—that person; brahma-yoga yukta-ātmā—those who are united with God through yog; sukham—happiness; akṣhayam—unlimited; aśhnute—experiences

translation.english: With the mind unattached to external contacts, finding delight in the Self, the Brahma-yogi enjoys imperishable happiness.
translation.hindi: बाह्य स्पर्शों में अनासक्त मन, आत्मा में जो सुख पाता है—वही ब्रह्म-योगयुक्त आत्मा अक्षय सुख भोगता है।

explanation.english: Turning inward shifts the centre of pleasure from fleeting objects to inexhaustible Being.
explanation.hindi: दृष्टि भीतर घुमाने से सुख का केन्द्र क्षणभंगुर वस्तुओं से असीम आत्म-सत्ता में सरक जाता है।

verses.sanskrit:
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते।

आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः।।5.22।।
verses.transliteration:
ye hi sansparśha-jā bhogā duḥkha-yonaya eva te
ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣhu ramate budhaḥ
verses.wordMeanings: ye—which; hi—verily; sansparśha-jāḥ—born of contact with the sense objects; bhogāḥ—pleasures; duḥkha—misery; yonayaḥ—source of; eva—verily; te—they are; ādya-antavantaḥ—having beginning and end; kaunteya—Arjun, the son of Kunti; na—never; teṣhu—in those; ramate—takes delight; budhaḥ—the wise

translation.english: Pleasures born of sense-contact are wombs of pain; they have a beginning and an end, O son of Kunti, and the wise do not delight in them.
translation.hindi: संवर्ग-संपर्क से उत्पन्न भोग दुःख की योनियाँ हैं; उनका आदि-अन्त है, हे कुन्तीपुत्र, अतः बुद्धिमान उनमें रमता नहीं।

explanation.english: Transient highs seed future lows; wisdom looks beyond this pendulum.
explanation.hindi: क्षणिक उछालें भविष्य के पतन बोती हैं; विवेक इस झूले से परे देखता है।

verses.sanskrit:
शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात्।

कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः।।5.23।।
verses.transliteration:
śhaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṁ prāk śharīra-vimokṣhaṇāt
kāma-krodhodbhavaṁ vegaṁ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ
verses.wordMeanings: śhaknoti—is able; iha eva—in the present body; yaḥ—who; soḍhum—to withstand; prāk—before; śharīra—the body; vimokṣhaṇāt—giving up; kāma—desire; krodha—anger; udbhavam—generated from; vegam—forces; saḥ—that person; yuktaḥ—yogi; saḥ—that person; sukhī—happy; naraḥ—person

translation.english: He who can withstand, here before liberation from the body, the urges born of desire and anger—he is a yogi, he is a happy man.
translation.hindi: जो शरीर के छूटने से पूर्व काम-क्रोध के उद्भूत वेग को सह सकता है, वही युक्त, वही सुखी मनुष्य है।

explanation.english: Mastery must be proven in the furnace of embodied life, not postponed to heaven.
explanation.hindi: स्व-नियंत्रण देहधारी जीवन की भट्टी में सिद्ध होना चाहिए, स्वर्ग के लिये टाला नहीं जा सकता।

verses.sanskrit:
योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः।

स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति।।5.24।।
verses.transliteration:
yo 'ntaḥ-sukho 'ntar-ārāmas tathāntar-jyotir eva yaḥ
sa yogī brahma-nirvāṇaṁ brahma-bhūto 'dhigachchhati
verses.wordMeanings: yaḥ—who; antaḥ-sukhaḥ—happy within the self; antaḥ-ārāmaḥ—enjoying within the self; tathā; antaḥ-jyotiḥ—illumined by the inner light; eva—certainly; yaḥ—who; saḥ; yogī—yogi; brahma-nirvāṇam—liberation from material existence; brahmabhūtaḥ— united with the Lord; adhigachchhati—attains

translation.english: He who finds joy within, who sports within, who is illumined within—such a yogi attains Brahma-nirvāṇa and becomes Brahman.
translation.hindi: जो अन्तर्य सुख पाता है, अन्तर्य रमण करता है, अन्तर्य ज्योति है—वह योगी ब्रह्म-निर्वाण को प्राप्त होकर ब्रह्मस्वरूप हो जाता है।

explanation.english: Inward-turned bliss flowers into identity with the source itself.
explanation.hindi: अन्तर्मुखी आनन्द स्वयं स्रोत के साथ तादात्म्य में खिलता है।

verses.sanskrit:
लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः।

छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः।।5.25।।
verses.transliteration:
labhante brahma-nirvāṇam ṛiṣhayaḥ kṣhīṇa-kalmaṣhāḥ
chhinna-dvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ
verses.wordMeanings: labhante—achieve; brahma-nirvāṇam—liberation from material existence; ṛiṣhayaḥ—holy persons; kṣhīṇa-kalmaṣhāḥ—whose sins have been purged; chhinna—annihilated; dvaidhāḥ—doubts; yata-ātmānaḥ—whose minds are disciplined; sarva-bhūta—for all living entities; hite—in welfare work; ratāḥ—rejoice

translation.english: Placeholder—Verse 25 standard text: ‘Those sages whose sins have been destroyed, whose doubts are cut, who are self-restrained and delight in the good of all beings, attain Brahma-nirvāṇa.’ (Authentic Sanskrit preserved in canonical editions.)

explanation.english: Verse 25 continues the theme: compassion plus inner purity equals immediate liberation.
explanation.hindi: पदानुसार, श्लोक 25 की धुरी यही है—करुणा और आन्तरिक शुद्धि का मेल तुरन्त मुक्ति देता है।

verses.sanskrit:
कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम्।

अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम्।।5.26।।
verses.transliteration:
kāma-krodha-viyuktānāṁ yatīnāṁ yata-chetasām
abhito brahma-nirvāṇaṁ vartate viditātmanām
verses.wordMeanings: kāma—desires; krodha—anger; vimuktānām—of those who are liberated; yatīnām—of the saintly persons; yata-chetasām—those self-realized persons who have subdued their mind; abhitaḥ—from every side; brahma—spiritual; nirvāṇam—liberation from material existence; vartate—exists; vidita-ātmanām—of those who are self-realized

translation.english: For the disciplined ascetics who are free from desire and anger, who know the Self, Brahma-nirvāṇa surrounds them on every side.
translation.hindi: जो यती काम-क्रोध से रहित, मन नियंत्रित, आत्म-ज्ञानी हैं, उनके四 ओर ब्रह्म-निर्वाण व्याप्त रहता है।

explanation.english: Liberation becomes the field they move in—no special moment required.
explanation.hindi: मुक्ति उनका चलायमान क्षेत्र हो जाती है—कोई अलग क्षण नहीं चाहिए।

verses.sanskrit:
स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः।

प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ।।5.27।।
verses.transliteration:
sparśhān kṛitvā bahir bāhyānśh chakṣhuśh chaivāntare bhruvoḥ
prāṇāpānau samau kṛitvā nāsābhyantara-chāriṇau
 yatendriya-mano-buddhir munir mokṣha-parāyaṇaḥ
vigatechchhā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ
verses.wordMeanings:
sparśhān—contacts (through senses); kṛitvā—keeping; bahiḥ—outside; bāhyān—external; chakṣhuḥ—eyes; cha—and; eva—certainly; antare—between; bhruvoḥ—of the eyebrows; prāṇa-apānau—the outgoing and incoming breaths; samau—equal; kṛitvā—keeping; nāsa-abhyantara—within the nostrils; chāriṇau—moving; 
 yata—controlled; indriya—senses; manaḥ—mind; buddhiḥ—intellect; muniḥ—the sage; mokṣha—liberation; parāyaṇaḥ—dedicated; vigata—free; ichchhā—desires; bhaya—fear; krodhaḥ—anger; yaḥ—who; sadā—always; muktaḥ—liberated; eva—certainly; saḥ—that person

translation.english: Shutting out external contacts, fixing the gaze between the brows, making the inhalation and exhalation flow evenly through the nostrils—
translation.hindi: बाह्य स्पर्शों को बाहर कर, दृष्टि को भ्रूमध्य में स्थिर कर, प्राण और अपान को नासिका-मार्ग से समान कर—

explanation.english: Krishna sketches the classic meditative posture preparing for samādhi.
explanation.hindi: कृष्ण समाधि की तैयारी हेतु पारम्परिक ध्यान-मुद्रा का रेखाचित्र देते हैं।

verses.sanskrit:
यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः।

विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः।।5.28।।
verses.transliteration: yatendriya-mano-buddhir  munir   mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ vigatecchā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā    mukta   eva saḥ
verses.wordMeanings: yata—controlled;   indriya—senses; manaḥ—mind; buddhiḥ—intelligence;   muniḥ—the   transcendentalist;  mokṣa—liberation;   parāyaṇaḥ—being so  destined;   vigata—discarded;   icchā—wishes;   bhaya—fear; krodhaḥ—anger;  yaḥ—one who;    sadā—always;    muktaḥ—liberated;   eva—certainly;  saḥ—he  is

translation.english: With senses, mind, and intellect subdued, the sage intent on liberation, free from desire, fear, and anger, is forever free.
translation.hindi: इन्द्रिय-मन-बुद्धि को संयमित कर, मुक्ति-परायण मुनि, इच्छा-भय-क्रोध से रहित, सदा के लिए मुक्त है।

explanation.english: Freedom is a present fact when reactivity ends, not a future reward.
explanation.hindi: प्रतिक्रिया-शून्यता आते ही मुक्ति वर्तमान सत्य बन जाती है, कोई भावी पुरस्कार नहीं।

verses.sanskrit:
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्।

सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति।।5.29।।
verses.transliteration:
bhoktāraṁ yajña-tapasāṁ sarva-loka-maheśhvaram
suhṛidaṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ jñātvā māṁ śhāntim ṛichchhati
verses.wordMeanings: bhoktāram—the enjoyer; yajña—sacrifices; tapasām—austerities; sarva-loka—of all worlds; mahā-īśhvaram—the Supreme Lord; su-hṛidam—the selfless Friend; sarva—of all; bhūtānām—the living beings; jñātvā—having realized; mām—me (Lord Krishna); śhāntim—peace; ṛichchhati—attains

translation.english: Knowing Me as the enjoyer of sacrifice and austerity, the great Lord of all worlds, and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
translation.hindi: यज्ञ-तपों का भोक्ता, समस्त लोकों का महेश्वर तथा सभी प्राणियों का सुहृद् मुझे जानकर मनुष्य शान्ति प्राप्त करता है।

explanation.english: The final key: recognise Krishna as beneficent centre of the universe and of one’s own heart—peace descends.
explanation.hindi: अन्तिम सूत्र: कृष्ण को विश्व-केन्द्र और हृदय-मित्र रूप में जानो—शांति उतर आती है।
